claims.text: Small red bumps around the mouth that often spare a thin rim of skin next to the lips
claims.quote: The immediate peri-vermillion skin is often spared, only rarely is it affected in severe cases.

claims.text: The most common association is steroid use by any route, including creams, inhalers and nasal sprays; cosmetics are another trigger
claims.quote: Steroid use via all routes (topical, inhaled, nasal insufflation) is the most common association.

claims.text: Mostly affects women aged about 20 to 45; slightly more common with lighter skin; also occurs in men and children
claims.quote: usually affects young to middle-aged women (20–45 years). ... slightly more common in lighter-skinned females

claims.text: Zero therapy is the first treatment; the rash may flare as the steroid is withdrawn
claims.quote: A flare may occur on discontinuation — steroids should not be restarted.

claims.text: Treatment usually runs 4 to 8 weeks, sometimes longer; recurrence can occur if treatment is too short
claims.quote: duration is usually 4–8 weeks but may require an extension ... Recurrence can occur if treatment is too short.

claims.text: Chronic inflammatory rash of small red bumps, sometimes with pus-filled heads, around the mouth and nose
claims.quote: Clusters of skin-coloured to red papules, vesicles, and pustules ... around the eyes, nostrils, mouth, and occasionally the genitals

claims.text: More severe cases can extend to the chin, cheeks, eyelids and forehead
claims.quote: more severe POD may extend to the chin, cheeks, lateral lower eyelids, upper eyelids, forehead, and glabella.

claims.text: Because it can also appear around the nostrils and eyes it is also called periorificial dermatitis
claims.quote: Periorificial dermatitis (POD) is a relatively common chronic inflammatory skin eruption. ... around the eyes, nostrils, mouth, and occasionally the genitals

claims.text: The single most important trigger is topical corticosteroids
claims.quote: Steroid use via all routes (topical, inhaled, nasal insufflation) is the most common association.

claims.text: Steroids from any route have been linked, including asthma inhalers and nasal sprays
claims.quote: Steroid use via all routes (topical, inhaled, nasal insufflation) is the most common association.

claims.text: Other triggers: cosmetics, toothpaste and dental fillings, thick paraffin- or petroleum-based moisturizers
claims.quote: Allergens/irritants eg, toothpaste and dental fillings. ... Occlusive emollient use leading to overhydration eg, paraffin or petroleum-based emollients

claims.text: Hormonal changes linked to birth control pills, pregnancy and premenstrual flares have been observed
claims.quote: Hormonal changes caused by oral contraceptive use, pregnancy, and premenstrual flares have been observed.

claims.text: In children it is often seen between 7 months and 13 years
claims.quote: However, it is also seen in young children, often between 7 months to 13 years old.

claims.text: It has no effect on overall health
claims.quote: Periorificial dermatitis is a benign self-limiting condition with no systemic consequences.

claims.text: Bumps on a red, slightly scaly background around the mouth and nasal folds
claims.quote: Erythematous base with a sharp border ... Scaly and flaky skin surface

claims.text: Each bump usually under 2 millimeters; clear band against the lip edge
claims.quote: Usually less than 2mm each; may coalesce into larger lesions

claims.text: Zero therapy: stop topical steroids, cosmetics and products, wash with warm water alone, bland preservative-free moisturizer
claims.quote: Preferably wash the face with warm water alone until the rash clears ... A bland emollient without preservatives/additives can be used for skin dryness.

claims.text: In mild cases zero therapy may be enough on its own
claims.quote: The zero-therapy approach should be utilised in all POD patients and may result in complete resolution of mild cases.

claims.text: Do not stop prescribed inhaled, nasal or oral steroids; medically necessary ones should be continued though they can slow recovery
claims.quote: Medically necessary nasal, inhaled, and oral steroids should be continued but will increase recovery time.

claims.text: Taper slowly over weeks, switching to a lower-potency steroid before stopping, substituting pimecrolimus
claims.quote: Slowly wean steroids over weeks, switching to a lower potency steroid before cessation ... substituting with topical pimecrolimus

claims.text: Do not restart the steroid once stopped
claims.quote: A flare may occur on discontinuation — steroids should not be restarted.

claims.quote: Metronidazole 0.75–1% ... Erythromycin 1% ... Pimecrolimus 1% twice daily for up to 4 weeks

claims.text: Tacrolimus has more limited evidence
claims.quote: Other topical therapies have limited evidence supporting efficacy and safety. These include: ... Tacrolimus

claims.text: Tetracycline is the recommended first-line oral choice and the response is usually quick
claims.quote: Tetracycline — recommended first-line, and the response is usually quick

claims.text: Treatment usually lasts 4 to 8 weeks but may need to be extended
claims.quote: duration is usually 4–8 weeks but may require an extension

claims.text: For pregnant women and children under 8, erythromycin is the first-line oral choice
claims.quote: Erythromycin — first-line for pregnant women and children under 8 years

claims.text: For very resistant cases oral isotretinoin can be considered, low-level evidence
claims.quote: Isotretinoin — low-level evidence for refractory cases.

claims.quote: The evidence supporting topical metronidazole ... is relatively weak and supported only by case series and a trial showing it to be inferior to tetracycline.
